To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of unilateral electromyography superimposed on volitional training (EVT) on maximal voluntary (MV) force and cross-sectional area (CSA) are equal to those of unilateral voluntary training (VT) on MV force and CSA, while EVT is more effective than VT in inducing cross-education of strength.

unilateral voluntary contraction and electromyostimulated voluntary contraction are equally effective in increasing muscle cross‐sectional areas and strength, and that the latter has the additional advantage of a larger cross‐education effect.

(i) unilateral voluntary training increases strength and CSA only in the trained leg, (ii) unilateral voluntary training combined with unilateral electrical stimulation increases strength and CSA in the untrained leg, and (iii) unilateral voluntary training without electrical stimulation combined with bilateral electrical stimulation increases strength only in the trained legs, while unilateral voluntary training combined bilateral electrical stimulation increases both strength and CSA in both trained and untrained legs.
